subject: Transportation Systems
title: Rush Hour Engineering
description: A 60-second lesson on Rush Hour Engineering.

hook.text: A subway built for average demand would collapse during rush hour. Peak capacity defines everything.

buildup.text: Morning and evening spikes can triple ridership. Trains run every 90 seconds on busy lines.

discovery.text: Operators stage extra trains, open additional exits, and deploy staff at chokepoints.

twist.text: Covid changed the pattern. Remote work flattened peaks, but evening and weekend ridership grew.

climax.text: Transit planners are redesigning schedules for a post-peak world where demand is more spread out.

punchline.text: Rush hour shaped the subway. Now it's dissolving.

quiz.question: How has remote work affected subway ridership patterns?
options: Flattened peaks and spread demand more evenly
